title: Leaked news release announces Konrad Narth will lead Manitoba PCs into election — before members vote
summary: The Manitoba NDP obtained a leaked draft of a Progressive Conservative news release announcing Konrad Narth would lead the Tories into the 2027 election — before the party's executive council even…

image.caption: Interim Progressive Conservative Leader Konrad Narth is shown in a file photo. He says he has 'serious concerns about the safety and protection of the party's files' after Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew presented a leaked draft news release in question period Thursday. (Kevin Nepitabo/CBC)

blocks.text: Manitoba·Updated

The Manitoba NDP obtained a leaked draft of a Progressive Conservative news release announcing Konrad Narth would lead the Tories into the 2027 election — before the party's executive council even voted on the possibility.
Draft Tory document says party's executive council swayed by Saturday meeting that hasn't happened yet

The Manitoba NDP obtained a leaked draft of a Progressive Conservative news release announcing Konrad Narth would lead the Tories into the 2027 election — even though the party's executive council hasn't voted on it yet.

Premier Wab Kinew presented a copy of a PC news release, dated two days in advance, during question period Thursday. It said the Tories' executive council passed a motion on that upcoming date endorsing Narth, the interim leader, to remain in the role during the next election campaign.

The release quoted party president Peter Smith as saying council was swayed by arguments that rushing a leadership race before a potential snap provincial election could lead PC members "to question the integrity of the process."

It said a leadership race would draw money, staff and volunteer capacity away from the party's goal of winning the next provincial election, which is scheduled for Oct. 5, 2027, but may be called sooner.
"We cannot hold a leadership race and prepare for a general election in the same year," the news release states in part.
Kinew slammed the Tories over the leaked document, alleging party brass was overriding their members by presupposing an outcome from an executive meeting that hadn't happened yet.
"What a charade. What an absolute mockery," the premier said.
Multiple releases being drafted: PC
Narth, who was appointed interim leader in September following the resignation of Obby Khan, said he was "blindsided" that a confidential party document would land in the premier's hands.

He said he left question period early to learn about the document. He made some phone calls and found the party was preparing multiple news releases for various potential outcomes stemming from Saturday's meeting, he said.

"I'd only assume that the premier had access to all of them and chose [the one] that would be the most controversial" to release, Narth said, adding he has "serious concerns about the safety and protection of the party's files, for sure."

blocks.text: The interim Tory leader said he wasn't aware of these news releases because he is intentionally staying out of all decisions surrounding the party's next leader. He continues to maintain he won't run for permanent leader whenever the race is called.
Also on Thursday, Narth said he learned there's been discussion of a resolution at Saturday's meeting that "would have an outcome similar to that [leaked news] release."

He maintained Saturday's executive council meeting to discuss the upcoming leadership race would still go ahead, with the ultimate decision left to the MLAs, election candidates and board members, among others, who comprise the council. Narth said he wouldn't participate.

Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew said the Opposition Tories are robbing their party members of the right to vote for the next leader by dictating the outcome in a news release. (John Woods/The Canadian Press)

The leaked news release derailed the Progressive Conservatives' plans for question period Thursday. Instead, Kinew spent the duration of the sitting turning Tory questions into digs at the party's elite for allegedly rigging the leadership process.
Kinew said the PCs were robbing the grassroots of their right to choose a leader.

"The current PC Party caucus stole the leadership from the member for Fort Whyte," Kinew said, referring to Khan, who said he stepped down because he didn't want to fight the caucus members he alleged were conspiring to remove him. He now sits as an Independent MLA.
"And now there is a conspiracy in the upper echelons of the PC Party of Manitoba to steal the right to choose the [leader] from you, the membership of the PC Party," Kinew added.

items: Tory interim leader Konrad Narth 'in it to win' if Manitoba election call comes early, he says

blocks.text: The party's president, Peter Smith, said Kinew's allegations are false.
"It is common practice to draft multiple press releases when there are multiple outcomes possible," he said in a statement.
"It is deeply disturbing to see political actors engaging in what is clearly theft and probably digital espionage."

Earlier in the day, Smith, in an interview with CBC News, wouldn't answer if there was a movement in the executive council to keep Narth as leader through the 2027 election because he said he didn't want to influence what is ultimately decided. However, he said party members have been happy with the PCs' direction under Narth.
Narth has previously said he would take the Tories into the next election if it happens before a leadership race plays out.
Kinew hasn't ruled out an earlier election date, but said delivering a balanced budget in the spring is the last major thing he wants to deliver before asking Manitobans for another mandate.

Ian Froese covers the Manitoba Legislature and provincial politics for CBC News in Winnipeg. He serves as president of the legislature's press gallery. He studied U.S. culture, media and politics as a 2025 World Press Institute fellow. You can reach him at ian.froese@cbc.ca.
